text: Plant action potentials differ from animal neuronal action potentials in their ionic basis. What ion fluxes primarily underlie the plant action potential?
choices: Sodium influx and potassium efflux, exactly as in animal neurons
Proton influx alone, with no other ions involved
Magnesium influx driven directly by ATP hydrolysis
explanation: Plant action potentials are all-or-nothing propagating events based on calcium influx and chloride efflux, in contrast to the sodium/potassium fluxes of animal neurons, and they travel through phloem sieve tubes at roughly 1 to 40 cm/s. The sodium/potassium account (choice 0) describes animal neurons, while proton-only (choice 2) and magnesium-driven (choice 3) mechanisms are not how plant action potentials work.
